name: Munnar
description: Kerala's best-known hill station at about 1,600 m: endless rolling tea estates, misty peaks around Anamudi (South India's highest), and Eravikulam National Park, home of the endangered Nilgiri tahr.
howToReach:
• From Kochi: NH85 via Kothamangalam and Adimali, ~130 km, 4 hrs.
• Nearest airport: Cochin International (COK), ~110 km.
• Nearest railheads: Aluva / Ernakulam, then KSRTC bus or taxi.
• KSRTC buses run from Ernakulam, Kottayam and Thekkady.
guide:
Day 1: Drive up via Cheeyappara and Valara waterfalls, Tata Tea Museum, sunset at a tea-estate viewpoint.
Day 2: Eravikulam National Park (Rajamala) in the morning, then Mattupetty Dam, Echo Point, Kundala Lake, Top Station.
Optional: 4x4 sunrise trip to Kolukkumalai from Suryanelli; Chinnar / Marayoor sandalwood forests and dolmens.
Stay: homestays and resorts in Chithirapuram, Pallivasal and Anachal are quieter than Munnar town.
tips:
• Eravikulam closes every year for Nilgiri tahr calving (roughly February–March) – check before going.
• Book Eravikulam tickets online; queues are long on weekends.
• Nights drop to 5–10 °C in Dec–Jan; carry a jacket.
• Neelakurinji blooms only once every 12 years (last 2018).
safety: Ghat roads are narrow with heavy fog in the evenings – avoid night driving. Landslide alerts are common in the monsoon (Jun–Aug). Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108, Kerala Tourism helpline 1800 425 4747.
photoCredits:
Munnar Overview.jpg – Kondephy, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Eravikulam National Park (49444006652).jpg – Mike Prince from Bangalore, India, CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Alappuzha Backwaters
description: The 'Venice of the East': palm-fringed canals, paddy fields below sea level and Vembanad Lake, best seen from an overnight kettuvallam houseboat with Kerala meals cooked on board.
howToReach:
• From Kochi: NH66, ~55 km, 1.5 hrs.
• Alappuzha railway station is on the Ernakulam–Kayamkulam coastal line.
• KSRTC buses every few minutes from Ernakulam and Thiruvananthapuram.
guide:
Overnight houseboat: board around noon at Punnamada / Finishing Point, cruise through Kuttanad, moor by evening, sunrise on the lake, disembark ~9 am.
Budget option: State Water Transport ferry Alappuzha–Kottayam (about 2.5 hrs, very cheap) or a shikara (small covered boat) for 2–3 hours.
Also: Alappuzha beach & pier, Marari beach (30 min north), Champakulam church.
Event: Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race – second Saturday of August on Punnamada Lake.
tips:
• Houseboats must stop cruising around 5:30 pm by rule – the overnight part is moored.
• Agree on what's included (meals, AC hours, cruise route) before paying.
• Prices drop sharply on weekdays and in the monsoon.
• Try karimeen (pearl spot fish) fry and toddy-shop food.
safety: Use operators with Kerala Tourism / Port Department registration and life jackets on board. Carry mosquito repellent. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108, Tourism helpline 1800 425 4747.
photoCredits:
Kerala Houseboat (191490747).jpeg – Kv Gopalakrishnan, CC BY 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Alappuzha Boat Beauty W.jpg – Augustus Binu/ facebook, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Kumarkom.jpg – Jigyasu, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Kumarakom
description: A cluster of islands on the eastern shore of Vembanad Lake with lakeside resorts, Ayurveda retreats and the Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary – quieter and more upmarket than Alappuzha.
howToReach:
• Kottayam railway station is 16 km away.
• From Kochi: ~75 km via Vaikom, 2 hrs.
• Ferries connect Kumarakom to Muhamma across the lake.
guide:
Early morning: Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary walk (migratory birds peak Nov–Feb).
Day: canoe or shikara ride through village canals, Ayurveda massage.
Evening: sunset over Vembanad from Pathiramanal island (boat from Muhamma / Kumarakom).
tips:
• Go to the sanctuary at opening time for birds.
• Many resorts offer village-life tours (coir making, toddy tapping).
• Kottayam town has cheaper stays if resorts are over budget.
safety: Lakes are deep – wear life jackets on small boats. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Kumarkom.jpg – Jigyasu, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Kerala Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary.jpg – P.K.Niyogi (talk), Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Fort Kochi & Mattancherry
description: Five centuries of Portuguese, Dutch, British and Jewish history on one walkable peninsula: Chinese fishing nets, St Francis Church, the Dutch Palace, the Paradesi Synagogue, spice warehouses, art cafés and the Kochi-Muziris Biennale.
howToReach:
• Cochin International Airport, ~45 km.
• Ernakulam Junction / Town railway stations, then ferry or Kochi Water Metro to Fort Kochi.
• State ferry from Ernakulam boat jetty is the cheapest and most scenic way in.
guide:
Morning: Chinese fishing nets at sunrise, St Francis Church, Santa Cruz Basilica, Princess Street.
Afternoon: Mattancherry Palace (Dutch Palace) murals, Jew Town antique shops, Paradesi Synagogue.
Evening: Kathakali performance (make-up session from ~5 pm), seafood grilled to order by the nets.
Biennale years: venues across Aspinwall House and Mattancherry (Dec–Mar).
tips:
• Mattancherry Palace is closed on Fridays; the synagogue closes Friday afternoons, Saturdays and Jewish holidays.
• Rent a bicycle – the area is flat and compact.
• Dress modestly for churches and the synagogue.
safety: Watch for traffic on narrow lanes; avoid isolated beach stretches late at night. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108, Tourism helpline 1800 425 4747.

name: Varkala
description: Kerala's only cliff-backed beach: red laterite cliffs above Papanasam beach lined with cafés, yoga shalas and Ayurveda centres, plus the 2,000-year-old Janardanaswamy Temple.
howToReach:
• Varkala Sivagiri railway station on the Kollam–Thiruvananthapuram line, then 10 min by auto.
• Thiruvananthapuram airport, ~50 km, 1.5 hrs.
guide:
Day 1: North Cliff walk at sunset, dinner at a cliff-top café.
Day 2: Morning yoga, Papanasam beach, Janardanaswamy Temple, Black Beach and Odayam beach.
Nearby: Kappil beach & backwaters (15 min), Ponnumthuruthu (Golden) island by canoe.
tips:
• Season shops and cafés open Oct–Apr; many close in the monsoon.
• Stay on North Cliff for nightlife, South Cliff for quiet.
• Cliff edges have no railings in places – careful after dark.
safety: Strong undertow – swim only between lifeguard flags; the sea is closed to swimming in the monsoon. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108, Tourism helpline 1800 425 4747.
photoCredits: Varkala Beach, Varkala, Kerala.jpg – Devender Goyal, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Kovalam
description: Three crescent beaches – Lighthouse, Hawa and Samudra – separated by rocky headlands just south of the capital, famous for Ayurveda resorts and the red-and-white Vizhinjam lighthouse.
howToReach:
• 16 km from Thiruvananthapuram city and ~15 km from the airport.
• Frequent city buses and autos from Thiruvananthapuram East Fort.
guide:
Morning: climb Vizhinjam lighthouse for the view, swim at Lighthouse beach.
Afternoon: Ayurveda massage, Hawa beach.
Evening: seafood on the promenade.
Nearby: Poovar estuary & golden sand beach by boat (~45 min south), Vizhinjam rock-cut cave temple.
tips:
• Ayurveda: choose centres certified by Kerala Tourism (Green Leaf / Olive Leaf).
• Prices are negotiable off-season.
safety: Swim only in lifeguard-marked zones; rip currents are common. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108, Tourism helpline 1800 425 4747.
photoCredits:
Kovalam beach trivandrum kerala.jpg – Georgeumartin, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Vizhinjam Light House.jpg – Akhilan, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Thekkady (Periyar)
description: Periyar Tiger Reserve around an artificial lake where elephants, gaur and sambar come to drink. Add spice plantations, bamboo rafting and Kalaripayattu shows in Kumily town.
howToReach:
• From Kochi: ~160 km via Kottayam / Kumily, 5 hrs.
• From Munnar: ~100 km, 3 hrs.
• Nearest airports: Madurai (~140 km) or Kochi.
guide:
Day 1: Arrive Kumily, spice plantation tour, evening Kathakali or Kalaripayattu show.
Day 2: First Periyar lake boat (around 7:30 am) for the best wildlife sightings; afternoon nature walk or bamboo rafting run by the Forest Department eco-tourism programme.
Optional: Chellarkovil viewpoint, Gavi eco-tourism (by KFDC package only).
tips:
• Book boat tickets online on the Periyar Tiger Reserve website – they sell out.
• Tiger sightings are rare; elephants and birds are common.
• Buy cardamom and pepper directly from estates.
safety: Stay with forest guides inside the reserve; leeches in the monsoon – carry salt / leech socks. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Periyar National Park.JPG – Wouter Hagens, Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
Thekkady.jpg – Jigyasu, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Wayanad
description: Misty plateau on the Western Ghats with coffee and spice estates, prehistoric carvings in Edakkal Caves, the heart-shaped lake on Chembra Peak, waterfalls and wildlife sanctuaries bordering Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
howToReach:
• From Kozhikode: up the Thamarassery Ghat (9 hairpins), ~75 km to Kalpetta, 2.5 hrs.
• Calicut International Airport, ~90 km.
• From Bengaluru: ~280 km via Mysuru, 6 hrs (forest checkposts close at night).
guide:
Day 1: Lakkidi viewpoint, Pookode Lake, Banasura Sagar Dam (India's largest earth dam).
Day 2: Edakkal Caves (steep climb), Soochipara or Meenmutty falls.
Day 3: Chembra Peak trek (forest permit, limited slots) or Muthanga / Tholpetty jeep safari.
tips:
• Edakkal Caves are closed on Mondays.
• Chembra and safaris need Forest Department permits – book early and check if open.
• Plantation homestays are the best way to stay.
safety: The July 2024 landslides devastated Mundakkai–Chooralmala; respect restricted zones and heed monsoon alerts. Wildlife on roads at night. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Edakkal Cave.jpg – നിരക്ഷരൻ at Malayalam Wikipedia., CC BY 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Athirappilly & Vazhachal Falls
description: Kerala's largest waterfall – about 25 m high and 100 m wide on the Chalakudy river – framed by rainforest. Vazhachal Falls is 5 km upstream.
howToReach:
• From Kochi: ~60 km via Angamaly and Chalakudy, 1.5–2 hrs.
• Chalakudy railway station is 30 km away; KSRTC buses run from Chalakudy.
guide:
Morning: top view of Athirappilly, then the forest path down to the base (15–20 min).
Then: Vazhachal Falls, Charpa Falls by the road.
Optional: continue on the forest road towards Valparai (checkpost timings apply), or the theme parks near Chalakudy.
tips:
• Most powerful in Jun–Sep, but entry to the base can close on high flow.
• Ticket counters close by late afternoon.
• No plastic allowed inside the forest area.
safety: Slippery rocks – never go near the edge or into the water. Elephants cross the Valparai road. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
The View of the Athirapally Falls during the onset of Monsoon.jpg – Jan Joseph George, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
The full flowing Vazhachal Falls on the upper reaches of Chalakudy River.jpg – Jan Joseph George, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Vagamon
description: A cool, uncrowded hill station of rolling grass meadows, pine forest and tea, known for paragliding and the Kurisumala hill ashram.
howToReach:
• From Kottayam: ~65 km via Erattupetta, 2 hrs.
• From Kochi: ~100 km, 3 hrs.
guide:
Morning: Vagamon meadows and pine forest, Thangal Para.
Afternoon: Vagamon Adventure Park (paragliding in season), Marmala waterfall.
Sunset: Kurisumala viewpoint.
tips:
• Weekdays are much quieter.
• Paragliding depends on the wind – book with licensed operators.
safety: Fog cuts visibility to a few metres in the evening. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Vagamon meadows.JPG – Visakh wiki, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Guruvayur
description: One of India's most important Krishna temples, plus Punnathur Kotta, the temple's elephant sanctuary. Nearby Thrissur hosts the spectacular Thrissur Pooram festival every April–May.
howToReach:
• Guruvayur railway station (branch line from Thrissur).
• Thrissur is 28 km; Kochi airport ~80 km.
guide:
Early morning darshan (queues are shortest at opening), Punnathur Kotta elephant sanctuary, Mammiyoor temple.
Combine with Thrissur: Vadakkunnathan temple, Shakthan Thampuran palace; time the trip with Thrissur Pooram if you can.
tips:
• Only Hindus may enter the main temple.
• Dress code: men in mundu, no shirt; women in saree, set-mundu or salwar.
• Weekends and wedding seasons are very crowded.
safety: Keep a safe distance from elephants at Punnathur Kotta. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Guruvayoor Temple 1.jpg – Susmitanair, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
009392022 Guruvayur temple, Kerala 004.jpg – Ms Sarah Welch, CC0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Bekal Fort
description: Kerala's largest fort – a 17th-century keyhole-shaped laterite fortress jutting into the Arabian Sea – with a beach park below and quiet Valiyaparamba backwaters nearby.
howToReach:
• Bekal Fort / Kanhangad railway stations, 5–10 min away.
• Mangaluru airport ~70 km; Kannur airport ~95 km.
guide:
Morning: walk the fort ramparts and observation tower, Bekal beach park.
Afternoon: houseboat or kayak on Valiyaparamba backwaters.
Optional: Ranipuram hill trek, Chandragiri fort.
tips:
• Sunset from the ramparts is the highlight.
• The north is far less touristy – stays are good value.
safety: Waves are strong below the fort walls. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Bakel Fort Beach Kasaragod7.jpg – Vinayaraj, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Valiyaparamba Madakkal suspension bridge.JPG – Alertedlevel2, CC BY 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Kozhikode
description: Calicut, the old spice port where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498, now Kerala's food capital – Malabar biryani, halwa, and snacks on SM Street, with a lively seafront.
howToReach:
• Calicut International Airport (Karipur), ~25 km.
• Kozhikode railway station on the main west-coast line.
guide:
Morning: Kappad beach (da Gama landing monument), Beypore – watch traditional wooden urus being built.
Afternoon: Mananchira Square, Tali temple, Mishkal Mosque.
Evening: SM Street (Mittai Theruvu) for halwa and banana chips, Kozhikode beach sunset, Malabar biryani dinner.
tips:
• Try kallummakkaya (mussels), pathiri and sulaimani tea.
• SM Street is busiest in the evening.
safety: Busy traffic; use licensed autos with meters. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Kozhikode Beach Coastline.jpg – Sulyab Thottungal, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Kappad Beach.jpg – SidhardhRamesh, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Kozhikode beach kites.jpg – Mr 037, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Kannur
description: The heartland of Theyyam, an ancient ritual dance performed in village shrines through the night, plus Muzhappilangad, a 4 km beach you can drive on, and the Portuguese-built St Angelo Fort.
howToReach:
• Kannur International Airport, ~30 km.
• Kannur railway station on the main west-coast line.
guide:
Day 1: St Angelo Fort, Arakkal Museum, Payyambalam beach.
Day 2: Drive Muzhappilangad beach, Dharmadam island at low tide.
Night: attend a Theyyam performance at a local kavu (shrine) – ask your homestay for the schedule.
tips:
• Theyyam season runs roughly November to May; performances are free – be respectful, no flash.
• Kannur is famous for handloom – buy at weavers' cooperatives.
safety: Drive slowly on the beach and stay above the tide line. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Kathivanoor Veeran Chemmarathi Thara-Eripuram.jpg – Uajith, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Muzhappilangad Drive-in Beach 2.jpg – Shagil Kannur, CC BY 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Kannurfort3.JPG – MANOJTV at en.wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Thiruvananthapuram
description: The capital: the gold-adorned Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, Kuthiramalika palace, the Indo-Saracenic Napier Museum, Shanghumukham beach and the Veli lagoon.
howToReach:
• Thiruvananthapuram International Airport (TRV).
• Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station.
guide:
Morning: Padmanabhaswamy Temple (Hindus only), Kuthiramalika palace museum next door.
Afternoon: Napier Museum, Sree Chitra Art Gallery, zoo.
Evening: Shanghumukham beach sunset, Veli tourist village.
Day trips: Kovalam, Poovar, Ponmudi, Neyyar Dam.
tips:
• Temple dress code is strict: men mundu and bare-chested, women saree or long skirt; dhotis can be hired at the gate.
• Phones and cameras are not allowed inside the temple – use the cloakroom.
safety: Heavy traffic on MG Road; use metered autos or ride-hailing. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108, Tourism helpline 1800 425 4747.
photoCredits:
Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple 01.jpg – Rahulrnath001, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Napier Museum South side 15 45 45 372000.jpeg – Shagil Muzhappilangad, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
0507-KuthiraMalika-Dinakarr.jpg – Dinakarr at English Wikipedia, Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Ponmudi
description: A compact hill station 1,100 m up, reached by a road of 22 hairpin bends through rainforest – a favourite day trip from the capital with misty views and streams.
howToReach:
• From Thiruvananthapuram: ~55 km, 1.5–2 hrs.
• KSRTC buses from Thiruvananthapuram Central.
guide:
Drive up early, stop at Kallar river and Golden Valley, walk to the Ponmudi top viewpoint, deer park.
Combine with Peppara Dam or Meenmutty falls hike (forest guide).
tips:
• The forest checkpost closes in the evening – plan to be down before then.
• The road can close after heavy rain; check before leaving.
safety: Monkeys snatch food – keep bags closed. Hairpins are tight; bikers should go slowly. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Morning at Ponmudi.jpg – Arunelectra, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Jatayu Earth's Center
description: A giant sculpture of the mythical bird Jatayu on a granite hilltop at Chadayamangalam – billed as the world's largest bird sculpture – reached by cable car, with an adventure park and wide views.
howToReach:
• From Thiruvananthapuram: ~50 km on MC Road, 1.5 hrs.
• From Kollam: ~38 km.
guide: Cable car up, sculpture and museum inside, sunset viewpoint. Add the adventure centre (rock climbing, zip line) if booked in advance.
tips:
• Book tickets online; cable car slots fill up on holidays.
• Climb up by the steps only if you're fit – it's steep.
safety: Rock surfaces get hot and slippery – wear proper shoes. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.

name: Silent Valley National Park
description: One of India's last undisturbed tropical evergreen rainforests, home to the lion-tailed macaque. Visits are only by Forest Department jeep to the Sairandhri watchtower.
howToReach:
• Drive to Mukkali via Mannarkkad (Palakkad district) – ~70 km from Palakkad, ~100 km from Coimbatore.
• Forest Department jeep from Mukkali to Sairandhri (~23 km).
guide: Reach Mukkali by 8 am, book the jeep safari at the information centre, Sairandhri watchtower and walk to the Kunthi river. Stay in Forest Department dormitories at Mukkali if available.
tips:
• Strictly no plastic and no private vehicles inside.
• Entry is restricted / closed in the peak monsoon – confirm with the Forest Department.
safety: Leeches in wet months; follow your guide. No mobile signal inside. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
SAN BIRDS 48.jpg – Sancia Morris, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Lion-tailed Macaque in Bristol Zoo.jpg – Chris huh, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Marari Beach
description: A quiet fishing-village beach 11 km north of Alappuzha with clean sand, casuarina groves and boutique homestays – the calm alternative to busier Kovalam and Varkala.
howToReach:
• Mararikulam railway station, 3 km.
• From Alappuzha: 20 min by car/auto.
• From Kochi: ~60 km on NH66, 1.5 hrs.
guide:
Morning: walk with the fishermen bringing in nets, swim in the calm early sea.
Afternoon: cycle the village lanes, coir-making units.
Evening: sunset on the beach; combine with an Alappuzha houseboat day.
tips:
• Few shops on the beach itself – most food is at homestays and resorts.
• Ask your host about fresh-catch dinners.
safety: No lifeguards on most stretches – swim close to shore; sea is rough in the monsoon. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Marari Beach Sunset 01.JPG – Mahendra M, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Sunset from Mararikulam beach, Kerala, India.jpg – Almost90's, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Cherai Beach
description: A long, gently shelving beach on Vypin island with the sea on one side and backwaters on the other, close to Kochi. Dolphins are sometimes spotted offshore.
howToReach:
• From Kochi: Goshree bridges to Vypin, ~25 km, 1 hr.
• Buses from Ernakulam High Court junction to Cherai.
guide: Beach in the morning, lunch at a backwater-side seafood shack, then Pallipuram fort (Ayikotta, built 1503) and Munambam fishing harbour for sunset.
tips:
• Weekdays are much quieter.
• Combine with Fort Kochi by taking the Vypin ferry.
safety: Swim only in flagged areas. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Sunrise at Cherai Beach.jpg – Jan J George, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Pallipuram Fort 2.jpg – KannanVM, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Poovar Island
description: Where the Neyyar river meets the sea near the Tamil Nadu border: mangrove channels, floating cottages and a golden sandbar beach reachable only by boat.
howToReach:
• From Thiruvananthapuram: ~30 km, 1 hr (via Kovalam).
• Boats leave from jetties at Poovar village.
guide: 1.5–2 hr boat ride through the mangroves to the golden sand beach and estuary; add a night in a floating cottage.
tips:
• Fix the boat fare and duration before boarding.
• Late afternoon light is best for photos.
safety: Don't swim at the estuary mouth – currents are strong. Wear life jackets. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Poovar Kerala.jpg – Midhun Subhash, CC0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Munroe Island
description: A cluster of islands where Ashtamudi Lake meets the Kallada river. Narrow canals, coir and prawn farming and everyday village life – best explored in a small country canoe.
howToReach:
• Mundrothuruthu railway station is on the island (Kollam–Kottayam line).
• From Kollam: ~25 km by road, 45 min.
guide: Early-morning canoe tour (around 3 hrs) through the canals, sunrise over Ashtamudi, toddy-shop lunch. Kollam town: Thangassery lighthouse and Kollam beach.
tips:
• Book the canoe with a homestay; start before 7 am.
• Carry a hat and water – canoes have no roof.
safety: Parts of the island are slowly sinking – stay on marked paths. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Beautiful Munroe Island , kollam district , kerala.jpg – Kkkriku, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Ashtamudi Kerala.jpg – The Raviz, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Thenmala Eco-tourism
description: India's first planned eco-tourism destination, in the forests of the Western Ghats: suspension bridge, nature trails, deer rehabilitation centre, boating on the Parappar reservoir and the Palaruvi waterfall nearby.
howToReach:
• On the Kollam–Shencottah road, ~70 km from Kollam, 2 hrs.
• Thenmala railway station on the Kollam–Sengottai line (scenic ghat section).
guide: Leisure zone (bridge, sculpture garden, musical fountain in the evening), adventure zone (rock climbing, rope walk), deer centre, then Palaruvi falls.
tips:
• Activities are sold as zone tickets at the entrance.
• The Punalur–Sengottai train ride through the hills is worth doing.
safety: Follow guides on forest trails; leeches in the wet season. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
13 kannara bridge near shencottah.jpeg – Tonymshaji6, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Palaruvi Waterfalls, thenmala - panoramio (1).jpg – Jaseem Hamza, CC BY 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Gavi
description: A remote forest and lake area inside the Periyar landscape with cardamom hills, elephants, gaur and Nilgiri tahr. Vehicle numbers are restricted, which keeps it pristine.
howToReach:
• Entry through the Vallakkadavu checkpost near Vandiperiyar (from Kumily/Thekkady side), with limited daily vehicle permits.
• KSRTC runs a daily bus from Pathanamthitta to Kumily via Gavi.
guide: Book a KFDC (Kerala Forest Development Corporation) package: trekking, boating on Gavi lake, wildlife spotting and an overnight stay in tents or the Green Mansion.
tips:
• Permits are limited – book days ahead and carry ID.
• No shops inside; fuel and cash before entering.
safety: Wild elephants on the road – never get out of the vehicle for photos. No mobile signal. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Gavi Eco tourism center kochupamba.jpg – Prasanth C7, CC0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Ilaveezhapoonchira
description: A treeless bowl of grassy hills at about 3,200 ft – the name means 'valley where leaves don't fall'. Sweeping 360° views, best at sunrise and sunset.
howToReach:
• From Kottayam: ~55 km via Erattupetta and Melukavu, 2 hrs.
• Last stretch is steep and rough; local jeeps run from the base.
guide: Sunrise or sunset on the ridge; add Illikkal Kallu rock (~10 km) for a short climb.
tips:
• Very windy – carry a light jacket.
• Few facilities: bring water and snacks.
safety: Thunderstorms in the afternoon in Apr–May and the monsoon – avoid the exposed ridge during lightning. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Illikkal Kallu (ഇല്ലിക്കൽ കല്ല് ).jpg – Hciteam1, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Ramakkalmedu
description: One of the windiest spots in India, on the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border, with wind turbines, a giant Kuravan–Kurathi sculpture and views down onto the plains of Tamil Nadu.
howToReach:
• About 15 km from Nedumkandam; ~40 km from Kumily/Thekkady.
• Easy add-on to a Thekkady or Munnar trip.
guide: Viewpoint and sculpture, short walk to the wind-farm ridge, sunset over Bodinayakanur plains.
tips:
• Hold on to hats and phones – gusts are strong.
• Combine with the Kalvari Mount viewpoint (Idukki reservoir).
safety: Stay behind railings near cliff edges. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Statue of Kuruvan & Kuruthi.jpg – Augustus Binu : flickr, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Marayoor
description: In the rain shadow of Munnar: Kerala's only natural sandalwood forest, prehistoric dolmens (muniyaras), traditional jaggery-making and the Chinnar wildlife sanctuary.
howToReach:
• From Munnar: ~40 km via Eravikulam/Rajamala road, 1.5 hrs.
• Buses from Munnar to Marayoor and Udumalpet.
guide: Sandalwood forest and government sandalwood outlet, Muniyara dolmens, a jaggery unit; afternoon Chinnar trek to Thoovanam waterfall (Forest Department guided).
tips:
• Buy jaggery and sandalwood only from government outlets.
• Chinnar treks need advance booking.
safety: Elephants in Chinnar – trek only with forest guides. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Kovilkadavu.jpg – {{subst:usernamexpand:Cyrillic}}, Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary.jpg – Matthieu Aubry, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Nelliyampathy
description: A cool plateau of orange, coffee and tea estates above the Palakkad plains, reached by a road with ten hairpin bends past Pothundy Dam.
howToReach:
• From Palakkad: ~60 km via Nenmara, 2 hrs.
• KSRTC buses from Nenmara.
guide: Pothundy Dam at the foot, drive up the ghat, Seetharkundu viewpoint, Kesavanpara, a plantation walk; jeep trip to Minnampara.
tips:
• Forest checkpost timings apply – start early, return before dark.
• Plantation bungalows are the main stays.
safety: Wildlife on roads after dusk; no fuel on top. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
The Western Ghats003.jpg – Shagil Kannur, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Pothundi dam palakkad.jpg – LIC Habeeb at Malayalam Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Malampuzha Dam & Gardens
description: Kerala's classic family day out: landscaped gardens below a large irrigation dam, a ropeway over the gardens, a snake park and Kanayi Kunhiraman's famous Yakshi sculpture.
howToReach:
• About 10 km from Palakkad town; Palakkad Junction railway station.
• Frequent town buses.
guide: Gardens and Yakshi sculpture, ropeway, boating, snake park, evening illumination. Add Palakkad Fort (Tipu's Fort) in town.
tips:
• Weekends and holidays are crowded.
• Evening lights are the highlight.
safety: Keep children away from the dam edges. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Malampuzha Dam Navas 10.jpg – Navas Puthanazhi, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Malampuzha Dam Area.jpg – Wikicd24, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Thusharagiri Falls
description: Three waterfalls on the Chalippuzha river in the Western Ghats foothills, with a forest trek to the highest, Thenpara, and good trekking to Vythiri beyond.
howToReach:
• From Kozhikode: ~50 km via Thamarassery and Kodenchery, 1.5–2 hrs.
• Buses from Kozhikode to Kodenchery, then local jeep.
guide: First falls near the entrance, forest trail to the second and Thenpara (allow 2–3 hrs). Combine with Wayanad via the Thamarassery ghat.
tips:
• Wear shoes with grip; trails are slippery after rain.
• Entry closes in the afternoon.
safety: Never bathe above the falls or in high flow. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Thusharagiri Waterfalls - തുഷാരഗിരി വെള്ളച്ചാട്ടം 09.jpg – Shijan Kaakkara, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Hill Palace Museum
description: The former seat of the Cochin royal family at Tripunithura, now Kerala's largest archaeological museum: royal regalia, the crown, oil paintings, manuscripts and a deer park on 52 acres.
howToReach:
• Tripunithura, ~12 km from Ernakulam; Kochi Metro to Tripunithura terminal, then auto.
• Tripunithura railway station.
guide: 2 hours for the galleries, then the deer park and heritage grounds. Combine with Fort Kochi on the same day.
tips:
• Kerala state museums are usually closed on Mondays.
• Photography rules vary by gallery.
safety: Low-risk; mind the steps between buildings. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Hill Palace by GV-1.JPG – Gokulvarmank, CC BY 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Kuruva Island
description: Uninhabited river islands in the Kabini covered in evergreen forest, crossed on bamboo rafts and stepping stones – a rare protected river ecosystem.
howToReach:
• About 17 km from Mananthavady; ~40 km from Kalpetta.
• Entry points at Pakkam and Palvelicham.
guide: Raft across, walk the forest trails between streams for 2–3 hrs. Combine with Thirunelli temple and Tholpetty safari.
tips:
• Daily visitor numbers are capped and access has been suspended at times – confirm it is open before going.
• Wear shoes you can get wet.
safety: Closed in the monsoon; stay on marked trails. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Kuruva Island Wayanad.JPG – Mrriyad, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Paithalmala
description: Kannur's highest peak (about 1,370 m) near the Karnataka border, reached by a forest trek through shola grassland to a watchtower with views over the Coorg hills.
howToReach:
• From Kannur: ~65 km via Taliparamba and Alakode, 2 hrs, to Pottanplavu at the base.
• Buses from Taliparamba to Pottanplavu.
guide: About 2 hrs up from Pottanplavu, watchtower and summit meadow, 1.5 hrs down.
tips:
• Start early to avoid afternoon mist.
• Carry water – none on the trail.
safety: Trek in a group; turn back in heavy fog. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits: Paithalmala.jpg – Rawbin, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Thattekad Bird Sanctuary
description: Dr Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary on the Periyar river – lowland evergreen forest famous for the Sri Lanka frogmouth, Malabar trogon and over 300 bird species.
howToReach:
• Near Kothamangalam, ~60 km from Kochi, 1.5–2 hrs.
• Buses to Kothamangalam, then local bus or auto.
guide: Dawn birding walk with a local guide (frogmouths roost by day), boat on the Periyar, Bhoothathankettu dam nearby.
tips:
• Local bird guides find species you'd never spot alone.
• Bring binoculars and neutral clothing.
safety: Elephants move through the area – go with a guide. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Ocyceros griseus -India-8a.jpg – Lip Kee Yap, CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
SriLankaFrogmouths.jpg – Shanthanu Bhardwaj, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Kerala Kalamandalam
description: The famous school of Kerala's classical arts at Cheruthuruthy on the Bharathapuzha – watch students train in Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Koodiyattam and percussion in traditional kalaris.
howToReach:
• About 30 km north of Thrissur; Vallathol Nagar railway station is next to the campus.
• Shoranur Junction is 5 km away.
guide: Morning: book the 'A Day with the Masters' visitor programme or watch classes, Koothambalam theatre. Afternoon: walk the Bharathapuzha riverbank.
tips:
• Classes run on working days during the academic year; vacations have no training to see.
• Ask before photographing students.
safety: Low-risk. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.
photoCredits:
Koothambalam at Kerala Kalamandalam.jpg – Arayilpdas at Malayalam Wikipedia, CC BY 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
Kathakali -Play with Kaurava.jpg – Bhoomi at Malayalam Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

name: Thrissur
description: Kerala's cultural capital, centred on the Vadakkunnathan temple and Thekkinkadu Maidan, home of Thrissur Pooram – caparisoned elephants, percussion ensembles and fireworks every April–May.
howToReach:
• Thrissur railway station on the main line; Kochi airport ~55 km.
• KSRTC buses from all major towns.
guide: Vadakkunnathan temple (Hindus only inside), Thekkinkadu Maidan walk, Shakthan Thampuran palace, Archaeological museum; Puli Kali (tiger dance) parade during Onam.
tips:
• Book stays months ahead for Pooram.
• Pooram crowds are enormous – pick a viewing spot early.
safety: During Pooram, keep clear of elephants and fireworks zones and follow police barricades. Emergency: 112, Ambulance 108.

വടക്കുംനാഥക്ഷേത്രം-തെക്കേഗോപുരം.jpg – Challiyan at Malayalam Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
